hypotheses.reasoning: Logins were healthy until 22:44 (#74, #79). The first anomaly is auth-svc's calls to the identity provider (idp.example/oauth2/token) slowing down: 4.2s (#77), then 7.7s (#80), then 30s timeouts (#84, #97). account-svc's AuthClient.issueToken timed out after 30s waiting on auth-svc (#85, #98). Those stuck calls filled account-svc's 50-connection pool to auth-svc (#101), new requests timed out waiting for a connection (#108), and edge-proxy returned 503s on /login (#96, #106, #114, #117). The DB, cache, and audit-consumer logs look normal, and no deploy shows up in the logs.

The slow endpoint is a third-party identity provider (idp.example). If the provider itself is degraded, this counts as an external outage. The only sign is rising latency followed by timeouts. No explicit error from the provider was logged.
The pool filling up in account-svc spread the failure to the edge. This is how the outage spread, not what started it.

verdict.recommendedAction: Check the identity provider's status page or contact the vendor. Give auth-svc a much shorter timeout on IdP calls (about 3–5s instead of 30s), plus a circuit breaker that fails fast. Lower account-svc's timeout to auth-svc to match. Add a limit (bulkhead) so slow token calls can't take all 50 connections in the auth-svc pool. If possible, serve a fallback while the IdP is degraded, such as reusing cached tokens or sessions.
